items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint with fp8 routed experts scores 10pp lower on AIME25 than vLLM (same weights, same node, same harness)
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [ ] **The bug persists in the latest version.** — See "Version note" below. This was measured on **v0.5.17**, not the latest v0.5.19. v0.5.19 requires `torch==2.13.0` while this deployment is pinned to `torch 2.11.0+cu130` to stay aligned with the training stack; I did not want to report numbers from an unsupported torch/sglang combination. Happy to re-run on v0.5.19 if you can confirm the expected torch/flashinfer pairing.
- [x] Environment info and reproduction details are included below.
- [x] This is a bug report, not a general question.
- [x] Written in English.

### Describe the bug

On the **same machine, same weights, same harness, same sampling parameters, same day**, SGLang scores **10.2 points lower than vLLM on AIME25** for a DeepSeek-V4-Flash checkpoint whose routed experts are **fp8**.

The official base model (fp4 routed experts) does **not** show this gap — it scores 95.83% under SGLang, in line with the ~96 reported in the SGLang cookbook. The gap appears only with the fp8-expert variant.

Runs were strictly sequential: SGLang was stopped and GPU memory fully released before vLLM was started, so the two never shared the GPUs.

#### Results — `sgl-eval run aime25`, 30 problems × 16 repeats = 480 samples

| | **SGLang 0.5.17** | **vLLM 0.28.0** |
|---|---|---|
| **pass@1[avg-of-16]** | **84.58%** ± 6.87 (SEM 1.72) | **94.79%** ± 4.21 (SEM 1.05) |
| majority@16 | 96.67% | 100.00% |
| pass@16 | 100.00% | 100.00% |
| **no_answer** | **4.17%** | **0.83%** |
| truncated_rate | 0.00% | 0.00% |
| error_rate | 0.00% | 0.00% |

The 10.2pp gap is far outside the SEM of either run.

#### The gap is mostly wrong answers, not lost answers

A natural first guess is that the parser is eating answers. Recomputing from the dumped predictions after excluding every `no_answer` case:

| | correct / answered | accuracy |
|---|---|---|
| SGLang | 406 / 459 | **88.45%** |
| vLLM | 455 / 476 | **95.59%** |

Still a **7.1pp** gap. So `no_answer` accounts for only about a third of the difference — the majority is the model producing *wrong* answers under SGLang. That points at the generation path rather than the parsing layer.

`truncated_rate` is 0.00% on both sides, so this is not a `max_tokens` artifact.

### The distinguishing factor: fp8 routed experts

This is the same model family and the same SGLang version that works fine on the official base weights. The only difference is the expert quantization:

| | This checkpoint (gap) | Official base (no gap) |
|---|---|---|
| `expert_dtype` | **`"fp8"`** | `"fp4"` |
| `quantization_config.scale_fmt` | **`"float"`** (F32 block scale) | `"ue8m0"` |
| `quant_method` | `fp8` | `fp8` |
| `weight_block_size` | `[128, 128]` | `[128, 128]` |

Tensor names and shapes are identical between the two; they differ only in expert dtype and scale dtype (verified by a header-by-header comparison).

SGLang detects this correctly at startup:

```
Auto-detected DSV4 routed-expert layout: is_fp4_experts=False
```

and routes to `Fp8MoEMethod` + DeepGEMM, which is the expected path. Loading succeeds, there are no warnings, and throughput is normal — the output is simply less accurate.

**The weights are from an internal fine-tune and cannot be shared**, but they were produced by `ms-swift`'s `megatron export` with `fp8_recipe=blockwise` + `fp8_param_gather`, which yields exactly the `expert_dtype=fp8` / `scale_fmt=float` combination above. Any DeepSeek-V4 checkpoint exported that way should reproduce this. If it would help, I can run additional diagnostics on this checkpoint on request (e.g. greedy decoding traces, per-layer activation dumps).

### Reproduction

Both servers were started on the same 8×H200 node, one at a time.

**SGLang** (no `--moe-runner-backend marlin` — marlin MoE only engages when `is_fp4_experts` is true; passing it with fp8 experts fails with `no attribute 'runner'`):

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001 \
  --tp-size 8 --trust-remote-code \
  --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --watchdog-timeout 1800 --enable-metrics
```

**vLLM** (official recipe, no extra env vars):

```bash
vllm serve /path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --served-model-name DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT \
  --trust-remote-code --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --no-enable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 --tool-call-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --enable-auto-tool-choice --reasoning-parser deepseek_v4 \
  --reasoning-config '{"reasoning_parser":"deepseek_v4","reasoning_start_str":"","reasoning_end_str":""}' \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8001
```

**Evaluation** — identical against both endpoints:

```bash
sgl-eval run aime25 \
  --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8001/v1 \
  --model DeepSeek-V4-Flash-SFT --api-key EMPTY \
  --n-repeats 16 --max-tokens 200000 \
  --temperature 1.0 --top-p 1.0 --thinking \
  --out-dir ./aime_out
```

### What I ruled out

Listing these so nobody re-treads the same ground:

1. **Chat template injecting tool scaffolding.** The model directory ships no `chat_template`, so each engine uses its own built-in. Measured `usage.prompt_tokens` on SGLang for a single-message request: **5 tokens** without `tools` vs **276** with one tool defined (the message itself is 1 token). So the no-tools template overhead is ~4 tokens — there is no hidden tool scaffolding in the prompt.
2. **`--moe-runner-backend marlin`.** Not applicable to fp8 experts (see above); auto-detection is doing the right thing.
3. **Truncation.** `truncated_rate` is 0.00% on both engines at `--max-tokens 200000`.
4. **`num_reasoning_tokens` reporting.** In the dumped predictions this is 0 for 100% of SGLang samples vs 0.21% for vLLM, which looks alarming but is unrelated: `sgl-eval` reads `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` (`sampler.py:172`), which SGLang does not populate. The reasoning content itself is still returned in `message.reasoning_content`.

### Environment

`python3 -m sglang.check_env` (version section; full NVIDIA topology omitted for length — 8×H200, NV18 all-to-all, 2 NUMA nodes):

```
Python: 3.12.13 | packaged by Anaconda, Inc. | (main, Jul  9 2026, 14:38:16) [GCC 14.3.0]
CUDA available: True
GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7: NVIDIA H200
GPU 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 Compute Capability: 9.0
CUDA_HOME: /usr/local/cuda
NVCC: Cuda compilation tools, release 12.9, V12.9.86
CUDA Driver Version: 590.48.01
PyTorch: 2.11.0+cu130
sglang: 0.5.17
sglang-kernel: 0.4.5
flashinfer_python: 0.6.15.post1
flashinfer_cubin: Module Not Found
flashinfer_jit_cache: Module Not Found
triton: 3.6.0
transformers: 5.12.1
torchao: 0.17.0
numpy: 2.3.5
huggingface_hub: 1.27.0
outlines: 0.1.11
xgrammar: 0.2.1
openai: 2.6.1
torchcodec: 0.11.1
ulimit soft: 1024
```

Comparison engine: **vLLM 0.28.0**, same node, same weights.

### Version note

Measured on v0.5.17. v0.5.19 declares `torch==2.13.0` and `flashinfer_python[cu13]==0.6.18`; this deployment is pinned to `torch 2.11.0+cu130` to match the training stack, and I did not want to report numbers from a hand-forced, unsupported combination. If you can confirm the intended torch/flashinfer pairing for v0.5.19 on H200, I'm glad to re-run the same comparison and post the numbers here.

items.title: [Bug] b12x-vision dev-v4f-2dgx regresses DSV4 history argument encoding from #28035
items.body:
## Summary

The `b12x-vision` branch at `452239a74f5b31798290f57aeac2645d98a52f44`, used by the two-DGX/GB10 DeepSeek V4 preview images, has regressed the `encoding_dsv4.py` portion of #28035.

The image commit is a descendant of the #28035 merge commit, and `serving_chat.py` still normalizes valid OpenAI assistant-history `function.arguments` JSON strings into dictionaries. However, `encode_arguments_to_dsml()` on this branch again calls `json.loads()` unconditionally. When it receives that already-normalized dictionary, the resulting `TypeError` is caught and the dictionary is wrapped as `{"arguments": original_dict}`. This encodes an incorrect extra DSML parameter layer.

## Affected branch and images

- Branch: `b12x-vision`
- SGLang commit: `452239a74f5b31798290f57aeac2645d98a52f44`
- ARM64 image digest: `sha256:03f2844f04c943aad743e36b8f8ce4716d1d0258c54de8503543fcc38aa48c87`
- Tags resolving to that digest:
  - `lmsysorg/sglang-staging:dev-v4f-2dgx`
  - `lmsysorg/sglang-staging:dev-cu13-v4f-2dgx`
  - `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-v4f-2dgx-v2`

The staging tags were last pushed on 2026-09-02; the public `-v2` alias was last updated on 2026-09-03.

## Minimal reproduction

This is the value passed to the DSV4 encoder after `serving_chat.py` has normalized a valid OpenAI history call:

```python
from sglang.srt.entrypoints.openai.encoding_dsv4 import encode_arguments_to_dsml

print(
    encode_arguments_to_dsml(
        {
            "name": "read",
            "arguments": {"filePath": "/tmp/example.txt"},
        }
    )
)
```

Actual output is equivalent to:

```xml
<｜DSML｜parameter name="arguments" string="false">{"filePath":"/tmp/example.txt"}</｜DSML｜parameter>
```

Expected output:

```xml
<｜DSML｜parameter name="filePath" string="true">/tmp/example.txt</｜DSML｜parameter>
```

Current branch logic:

```python
try:
    arguments = json.loads(tool_call["arguments"])
except Exception:
    arguments = {"arguments": tool_call["arguments"]}
```

The #28035 behavior accepts either the original JSON string or the already-normalized dictionary, then validates that the result is an object:

```python
raw_arguments = tool_call["arguments"]
arguments = (
    json.loads(raw_arguments) if isinstance(raw_arguments, str) else raw_arguments
)
if not isinstance(arguments, dict):
    raise ValueError(
        "Assistant tool call function.arguments must be a JSON object."
    )
```

## Impact

Valid multi-turn OpenAI tool histories are encoded back into the model prompt with an extra `arguments` wrapper. This can teach or induce DeepSeek V4 to emit the same invalid nested shape, causing downstream agents to reject otherwise valid tool calls because required schema fields appear to be missing.

## Relationship to #38386

#38386 repairs nested arguments emitted by the model in the DeepSeek tool-call detector. It is useful but is not a replacement for this fix: this regression corrupts valid assistant tool-call history while constructing the prompt, before output parsing happens.

## Requested fix

1. Restore the #28035 `encoding_dsv4.py` behavior on `b12x-vision`.
2. Add a branch regression test where `encode_arguments_to_dsml()` receives an already-normalized dictionary.
3. Publish a refreshed, preferably versioned two-DGX/GB10 image and update the DeepSeek V4 cookbook to its immutable digest.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1 fp8 wo_a absorb GEMM is silently ~25% wrong when DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0 is false (SM121)
items.body:
## Summary

On SM121 (GB10), the fp8 `wo_a` absorb GEMM in `deepseek_v4.py` returns results that are **~25% wrong, with no error**, whenever `deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0` is false. The non-ue8m0 branch hands `deep_gemm.fp8_einsum` per-token activation scales that are not powers of two; the kernel requires power-of-two scales and truncates the mantissa instead of rejecting them.

I hit this while enabling the path on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and isolated it on real checkpoint weights. I have only tested SM 12.1, so I make no claim about the sm90 path — but the branch is selected by a flag, not by architecture, so it looks reachable elsewhere.

## Where

`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`, in the fp8 `wo_a` branch (around line 2075):

```python
if deep_gemm_wrapper.DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0:
    # sm100 (Blackwell): ue8m0 scales via the dedicated JIT kernel.
    o_fp8, o_s = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8_dsv4_wo_a(o)
    recipe = (1, 1, 128)
else:
    # sm90 (Hopper): fp32 scales.
    o_fp8, o_s = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(
        o.reshape(T * G, D).contiguous(),
        group_size=128,
        scale_ue8m0=False,          # <-- produces non-power-of-two fp32 scales
    )
    ...
    recipe = (1, 128, 128)
output = torch.empty(T, G, R, device=o.device, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
deep_gemm.fp8_einsum("bhr,hdr->bhd", (o_fp8, o_s), (...), output, recipe=recipe)
```

`deep_gemm/include/deep_gemm/impls/smxx_layout.cuh:131` asserts

```
(values[j] & 0x807fffffu) == 0
```

i.e. sign and mantissa bits clear — the fp32 scale must be an exact power of two.

The important asymmetry: that check covers the **weight** scale, not the activation scale. Feeding deliberately non-power-of-two *weight* scales fires it loudly (`Assertion failed: ... smxx_layout.cuh:131`, repeated per block). Feeding non-power-of-two *activation* scales — which is exactly what `scale_ue8m0=False` produces — passes without a word and returns a wrong answer. So the requirement is enforced on one operand and silently assumed on the other.

## Isolation

Real `layers.20.attn.wo_a` from the DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint, sharded to TP4 rank 0 (`[2048, 4096]` fp8), G=2, R=1024, D=4096, T=6. Varying one operand's scale at a time against a dequantized fp32 reference:

| activation scale | weight scale | max rel err |
|---|---|---|
| unit | unit | 2.40e-03 (fp8 rounding floor — kernel is fine) |
| unit | real 128x128 blocks | 2.84e-03 (weight path fine) |
| **real, `scale_ue8m0=False`** | real | **2.52e-01** |
| **real, `scale_ue8m0=True`** | real | **2.50e-03** |

For reference the bf16 path this replaces measures 2.71e-03 on the same inputs, so `scale_ue8m0=True` is numerically equivalent to it and `False` is not remotely close.

Checking the scales directly:

```python
bits = o_s.view(torch.int32)
((bits & 0x807fffff) == 0).all()   # scale_ue8m0=False -> False
                                   # scale_ue8m0=True  -> True
```

## Suggested fix

Either force ue8m0 for this call regardless of `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0`:

```python
o_fp8, o_s = sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(
    o.reshape(T * G, D).contiguous(), group_size=128, scale_ue8m0=True)
```

or, if the non-ue8m0 scales are correct for some other backend, gate the branch on what `fp8_einsum` actually accepts rather than on `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0`.

Separately, it would be worth making that assert unconditional (or adding a host-side check) so a non-power-of-two scale fails loudly everywhere rather than degrading silently — the silence is what makes this expensive to find.

## Environment

- 4x DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1), TP4, EP2
- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `quant_method: fp8`, `scale_fmt: ue8m0`, `weight_block_size: [32, 32]`, MXFP4 experts
- `DEEPGEMM_SCALE_UE8M0` is **false** on this build, so the non-ue8m0 branch is the one taken
- deep_gemm with `fp8_einsum`; `ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=1`

## Note on reaching this path at all

On a `[32, 32]` block-scale checkpoint like this one, `wo_a_fp8_gemm_enabled` (`deepseek_v4.py:281`) requires `weight_block_size == [128, 128]`, so `wo_a` is dequantized to bf16 at load and the bug is unreachable. I got here by re-blocking the scales to 128x128 first, which for a ue8m0 checkpoint is close to exact (keeping each 4x4 group's max exponent and shifting the fp8 mantissas: max rel err 4.1e-06 across all 43 tensors, maximum shift 3 binades). That may be worth supporting directly — with it the absorb GEMM goes from 3.55 to 2.15 ms/step at bs=1 on this fleet — but it is a separate request from the correctness issue above.

items.title: [Bug] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash + Engram: profiled SPS table (compact ragged verify) dies in CUDA-graph capture with "engram target-verify expects one equal block per request"
items.body:
### Checklist

- [x] I searched related issues but found no solution.
- [x] The bug persists in the latest version.
- [x] Issues without environment info and a minimal reproducible demo are hard to resolve and may receive no feedback.
- [x] If this is not a bug report but a general question, please start a discussion at https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/discussions. Otherwise, it will be closed.
- [x] Please use English. Otherwise, it will be closed.

### Describe the bug

On DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (an Engram model), enabling DSpark compact ragged verify via a profiled SPS cost table makes the engine die **deterministically during CUDA-graph capture, on every rank**:

```
AssertionError: engram target-verify expects one equal block per request, got 42 tokens for 8 requests of 6
```

Removing the table (so the planner stays on the verify-all / static schedule) boots and serves fine, so weights, TP4/EP4, FP8 KV cache and the RDMA transport are all healthy.

**Suspected root cause.** The capture batch seems to get the wrong slot count. `DecodeCudaGraphRunner._ragged_capture_slots()` returns `min(num_tokens, self.max_bs)` (`model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:667-670`), while the per-tier token bucket is `bs * captured_req_width` (`_build_ragged_verify_token_buckets`, same file, line 569). For the tier `num_tokens = 42` (bs=7, width=6) with `max_bs = 8` this selects **8 slots**, so `build_capture_verify_lens(num_tokens=42, num_slots=8, num_draft_tokens=6)` returns `[6,6,5,5,5,5,5,5]` — 8 rows of unequal length summing to 42. `EngramHasher.forward()`'s target-verify branch (`srt/layers/engram.py:291-298`) requires one equal block per request (`num_tokens == bs * block` → `42 != 8*6`), so the capture batch is rejected. Only the largest tier (bs == max_bs → 48 tokens / 8 slots) survives; every smaller tier aborts. Dense-layout consumers elsewhere handle ragged layouts through `RaggedVerifyLayout.padded_to_bucket(padded_bs, cap)`, but the Engram hasher reads the raw `input_ids.shape[0]` / `req_pool_indices.shape[0]` pair before any padding.

The test escape hatch `SGLANG_TEST_RAGGED_VERIFY_FORCE_UNIFORM_CAPTURE=1` avoids the capture assertion but then dies on the first request (second traceback below), so compact ragged verify currently appears unusable for this model.

### Reproduction

**Model:** DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (native weights: MXFP4 experts / FP8 dense), Engram layer with per-rank shards on local NVMe.
**Hardware:** 4x NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, SM 12.1, 128 GB unified memory), TP4 + EP4, 200G RoCE.
**Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:dev-dsv41`, `org.opencontainers.image.revision = e087e662ba1ac4ef7747537e2a9141085efd4561`.

**Step 1 — profile the SPS cost table** against a running (table-less) server:
```
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.dspark_sps_profiler all --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8000
```
produced `/state/dspark_sps.json` (158 B):
```
{"sample_batch_tokens":[6,12,24,48],"sample_steps_per_sec":[16.247257259883817,12.474520791283801,8.601395834516026,5.8263395410067975],"max_batch_tokens":48}
```
manifest: `tp_size=4, dp_size=1, verify_num_draft_tokens=6, simulate_acc_len=1.0, batch_size_per_rank_sweep=[1,2,4,8]`.

**Step 2 — start the server with the table present** (`SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=compact`):
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --served-model-name deepseek-v4.1-flash \
  --tp-size 4 --ep-size 4 --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --context-length 1048576 --mem-fraction-static 0.90 --max-total-tokens 4000000 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-running-requests 8 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 8 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --speculative-dspark-sps-table-path /state/dspark_sps.json \
  --speculative-dspark-align-verify-tokens-to-graph-tier
```

**Step 3 — with `SGLANG_TEST_RAGGED_VERIFY_FORCE_UNIFORM_CAPTURE=1`** capture succeeds and the server boots, but the first decode request crashes:

items.title: [Bug] HiCacheFile reports an unrestorable prefix for hybrid cache pools
items.body:
## Describe the bug

`HiCacheFile.batch_exists_v2()` can report a hybrid prefix as a hit even when a required auxiliary pool cannot restore that prefix.

The file backend finds each pool's longest usable prefix and takes the minimum of those lengths. That works for contiguous `ALL_PAGES` coverage, but `TRAILING_PAGES` pools can have holes in their valid endpoints. For example, with all three KV pages present:

| SWA valid endpoints | Mamba valid endpoints | Expected shared endpoint | Actual |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `{3}` | `{3}` | 3 | 3 |
| `{3}` | `{2}` | 0 (no common endpoint) | 2 |
| `{1, 3}` | `{1, 2}` | 1 | 2 |

In the latter two cases, the reported endpoint has no SWA object. The last case also overlooks an earlier valid common checkpoint. The same problem occurs when an `ALL_PAGES` pool truncates a trailing pool to an endpoint that the trailing pool cannot serve.

The usable prefix should end at the greatest common legal endpoint, or zero if none exists. `MooncakeStore.batch_exists_v2()` already uses an intersection of legal endpoints.

This report establishes an incorrect backend existence-query result. It does not claim a reproduced model-output error or an end-to-end load-back failure. It is separate from #38452, which concerns whether the scheduler consults L3.

## Reproduction

Run this in a source checkout with SGLang's Python dependencies available. No model, server, accelerator or valid KV payload is needed: empty temporary files are sufficient for the existence-query contract. The constructor is bypassed to isolate the query from unrelated eviction setup; the query and filesystem scan methods are unmodified.

```python
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory

from sglang.srt.mem_cache.hicache_storage import (
    HiCacheFile, PoolHitPolicy, PoolName, PoolTransfer,
)

def query(swa_pages, mamba_pages):
    with TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
        backend = HiCacheFile.__new__(HiCacheFile)
        backend.file_path = directory
        backend.config_suffix = "_repro"
        backend.metadata_cache = None
        keys = ["p1", "p2", "p3"]
        for name, pages in (
            (PoolName.KV, {1, 2, 3}),
            (PoolName.SWA, swa_pages),
            (PoolName.MAMBA, mamba_pages),
        ):
            for page in pages:
                Path(backend._get_component_path(keys[page - 1], name)).touch()
        transfers = [
            PoolTransfer(
                name=name, keys=[keys[-1]],
                hit_policy=PoolHitPolicy.TRAILING_PAGES,
            )
            for name in (PoolName.SWA, PoolName.MAMBA)
        ]
        return backend.batch_exists_v2(keys, transfers).kv_hit_pages

actual = [query({3}, {3}), query({3}, {2}), query({1, 3}, {1, 2})]
print(actual)  # affected code: [3, 2, 2]
assert actual == [3, 0, 1]
```

## Environment

- Reproduced against `f618022b73f813daa6f25e615b0269c82c66a941`; the affected method is unchanged at `5f3606c7b2aec653fcfdbe3465379e700c4a5492`.
- macOS 26.6.2, Apple Silicon; Python 3.12.14; CPU Torch 2.13.0.
- Local validation imported the actual storage/environ modules through namespace packages to bypass SGLang's GPU-heavy package initialization. No storage-query method was replaced or extracted.
- Normal `python -m sglang.check_env` stops during package initialization with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'triton'`; therefore a full runtime environment report and GPU E2E result are not available.

I have a focused fix and CPU regression coverage ready. AI assistance was used for investigation and implementation.

items.title: [Bug] SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE mislabels capture traces and crashes with IndexError when a bs bucket captures multiple graphs
items.body:
### Describe the bug

`SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE` writes one chrome trace per decode CUDA graph
capture. The naming callback assumes each batch-size bucket captures exactly
one graph, which is not true for DSA dual-graph, LoRA / no-LoRA, or PDMUX.

On a DSA model the server fails to start with an `IndexError` raised from
inside the torch profiler. Worse, the traces written *before* the crash are
silently attributed to the wrong batch size, so the feature can produce
misleading data even where it does not crash.

`_init_profile_context_and_memory_record` names each flush by walking the bs
sequence with a cursor
([decode_cuda_graph_runner.py#L853](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py#L853)):

```python
def on_trace_ready(prof):
    bs = self._profile_bs_list[self._profile_bs_idx]
    self._profile_bs_idx += 1
    ...
```

But `_capture_one_stream` sweeps the LoRA and DSA variants *inside* the bs
loop, so the profiler flushes `len(capture_bs) * len(lora_variants) *
len(dsa_variants)` times, not `len(capture_bs)` times:

```python
for bs in capture_range:
    for variant_label, _variant_has_lora in lora_variants:
        for dsa_variant in dsa_variants:
            ...  # one capture -> one profiler flush
```

PDMUX hits the same coupling from the other side: `capture()` repeats the
whole sweep once per stream group, and each group would overwrite the
previous group's files even if the cursor did not run off the end first.

### Reproduction

```bash
SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4 --tp 8 \
  --trust-remote-code --enable-profile-cuda-graph \
  --cuda-graph-bs-decode 11 7 5 3
```

Observed on MI355X / ROCm, sglang 0.5.19 and main
(`76ef679cb1f720913b122c75f2da994641a3f38d`).

Any model where `dsa_dual_graph` is true works, i.e. ROCm plus an
architecture on the `is_deepseek_dsa` whitelist with `index_topk` set.
`amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4` is `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` with `index_topk=2048`. I
confirmed at config level that `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.2`
(`DeepseekV32ForCausalLM`, `index_topk=2048`) is classified the same way, so
it should reproduce identically; I did not run it.

Four batch sizes are enough. I used odd values so a bs can never be confused
with a head count or hidden dimension when reading a trace.

### Observed behavior

Capture dies partway through the third bucket:

```
Capturing batches (bs=5 avail_mem=56.07 GB):  50%|#####     | 2/4 [00:52<00:52, 26.42s/it]
[TP0] Scheduler hit an exception: Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 1308, in capture_one_shape
    self.backend.capture_one(
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/runner_backend/full_cuda_graph_backend.py", line 189, in capture_one
    profiler.step()
  File "torch/profiler/profiler.py", line 922, in _trace_ready
    self.on_trace_ready(self)
  File "sglang/srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py", line 853, in on_trace_ready
    bs = self._profile_bs_list[self._profile_bs_idx]
         ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
IndexError: list index out of range

Received sigquit from a child process. It usually means the child failed.
```

Four files are on disk when it dies, and three of them name the wrong bs.

This can be shown without trusting the names. Each trace carries a
`ProfilerStep#k` marker, and `capture_one` issues exactly three
`profiler.step()` calls against a `wait=2, warmup=0, active=1` schedule, so
flush *j* is stamped `ProfilerStep#(3j+2)`. That identifies which flush
produced each file. The `cuda_runtime` launch count then fingerprints the
graph, since the DSA sparse graph launches more kernels than the dense one:

| file written | `ProfilerStep#` | launch count | graph actually captured |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `..._bs_11_rank0.json.gz` | 2 | 6775 | bs=11 dense (correct, by luck) |
| `..._bs_7_rank0.json.gz` | 5 | 7333 | **bs=11 sparse** |
| `..._bs_5_rank0.json.gz` | 8 | 6766 | **bs=7 dense** |
| `..._bs_3_rank0.json.gz` | 11 | 7333 | **bs=7 sparse** |
| (5th flush) | 14 | — | bs=5 dense -> `IndexError` |

### Expected behavior

One trace per captured graph, named after the graph it contains. With four
batch sizes and DSA dual-graph that is eight files, and the server starts
normally.

### Environment

- MI355X / ROCm, sglang 0.5.19 and main @ `76ef679`
- `--enable-profile-cuda-graph` with `SGLANG_GRAPH_BATCH_CAPTURE=1`
- The LoRA / no-LoRA path (`record_nolora_graph`) and the PDMUX path have the
  same shape but I have not reproduced them on hardware; PDMUX is NVIDIA-only
  and I have ROCm only.

items.title: [Bug] Quantized DFlash2 draft silently yields ~0% acceptance — no error, no warning (the quiet counterpart to #36599)
items.body:
### Summary

A **quantized** DFlash2 draft checkpoint loads into `DFlash2DraftModel`, serves, and produces
drafts that are rejected ~100% of the time. There is **no error and no warning** — acceptance
simply collapses from ~3.7 to ~1.0 and decode drops below no-drafter speed.

The same weights **unquantized** work correctly. This is the silent counterpart to #36599 (quantized
NextN draft, `modelopt_fp4`), which fails loudly with a tensor-shape mismatch instead.

This is a read-only report — I have not root-caused it and am not opening a PR.

### Repro

Target: `Frozenlock/Qwen3.8-27B-int4-AutoRound` (auto-round, 4-bit, g128, sym).
Two drafters that are **the same model**, differing only in quantization:

| drafter | params | dtypes | quant |
|---|---:|---|---|
| `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` | 1,924,404,480 | BF16 | none |
| `syvai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2-W4A16` | 1,924,404,480 | I32 + BF16 | compressed-tensors |

Identical `architectures` (`DFlash2DraftModel`), identical `dflash_config`
(`block_size 8, selector_rank 256, selector_top_k 16`, same `target_layer_ids`), identical tensor
names including `candidate_selector.{hidden_projection.weight,predecessor_codebook,successor_codebook}`.

```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <qwen3.8-27b-autoround-int4> \
  --tp-size 2 --quantization auto-round --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --attention-backend flashinfer --context-length 262144 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.82 --max-running-requests 1 \
  --speculative-algorithm DFLASH \
  --speculative-draft-model-path <DRAFTER> \
  --speculative-draft-model-quantization <compressed-tensors | unquant>
```

### Result

| drafter | `accept len` | `accept rate` | decode (code) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| syvai (compressed-tensors) | **1.03** (n=422) | **0.004** | ~38 tok/s |
| z-lab (BF16, `unquant`) | **3.71** (n=100) | 0.61 | ~171 tok/s |

With the quantized drafter, `accept len` never exceeded **1.12** across 422 decode batches. At
`block_size 8` a working drafter reads 2–5. Decode is **slower than running with no drafter at
all**, because it pays full verify cost for zero accepted tokens.

### Why this is easy to miss

1. The draft loads into the correct class and logs success:
   `Load weight end. type=DFlash2DraftModel, quant=compressed-tensors`.
2. Speculative decoding **rejects** bad drafts, so correctness is preserved by construction — a
   0%-acceptance drafter is slow, never wrong. Output stays fluent and correct.
3. Our functional test suite reported **"All checks passed"** on the broken configuration
   (completion, tool calls, streaming, reasoning split, a 2K-token coherence check, vision).

The only signal is the engine's own `accept len:` / `accept rate:` counters in the decode-batch log.

### What I ruled out

- **Not an architecture-mapping failure.** `DFlash2DraftModel` is first-class
  (`srt/models/dflash.py:1066`) and listed in
  `model_executor/model_runner_components/spec_aux_hidden_state.py`.
- **Not the target's aux-hidden-state capture.** #38589 reports that gap for `Qwen4Exp` and
  explicitly names `qwen3_5.py` — our target — as the *working* parent.
- **Not tensor naming.** Byte-for-byte identical between the two checkpoints.
- **Not the target `lm_head`.** Ours is dense BF16, satisfying the DFlash2 selector's dense path.

### Leading hypothesis (untested)

The `CandidateSelector` codebooks / `hidden_projection` are loaded through the compressed-tensors
path and end up wrong — well-formed but not the trained values — so the selector emits confident
garbage. That would match the symptom exactly: loads clean, runs, drafts nothing acceptable.

### Suggested mitigation regardless of root cause

Warn (or refuse) when a DFLASH draft resolves to a quantized checkpoint, as #36599 suggests for the
NextN path. A one-line boot warning would have saved a full benchmark cycle here.

### Related

- #36599 — same class (draft quant config mishandled), NextN/`modelopt_fp4`, fails loudly.
- #38589 — DFlash aux-hidden-state capture on `Qwen4Exp`.
- #36118 — runs `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2` successfully (accepted span 4.49 @10K), consistent with
  the BF16 arm here.

### Environment

- SGLang `v0.5.19` (`lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19`), stock, no patches
- 2× RTX 3090 (sm_86), PCIe, no NVLink, TP=2, `--disable-custom-all-reduce`
- Downstream context: https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090 (SGLang tier for Qwen3.8-27B)

⚠️ One SGLang-specific footgun found while narrowing this down, in case it is worth documenting
separately: `--speculative-draft-model-quantization` defaults to the **target's** quantization when
unset (`arg_groups/serving_hook.py:629`). Pointing at a BF16 drafter without passing `unquant`
therefore applies the target's `auto-round` to BF16 weights and reproduces the identical
0%-acceptance symptom from the other direction.
